title: Personal and family details for pension fund registration
goal: Lonio collects every field Pensionskasse Muster requires, including the spouse's date of birth for married employees, so that a registration is never blocked by missing data.
context: The pension fund portal requires first name, last name, date of birth, canton and civil status for every employee (F-SC-002 to F-SC-007, F-SC-010, F-SC-015). For married employees it also requires the spouse's date of birth and blocks the registration without it (F-TR-021, F-SC-012 to F-SC-014, F-SC-016). The civil status list shows only Single, Married, Divorced and Widowed (F-SC-011, G-07). HR's recollection of civil status matches the fund's list (F-TR-020, F-TR-022). Civil status is also an input for the source tax rule and the calculator (F-TR-029, F-TR-030). The fund offers only Swiss cantons and does not say whether it means the canton of residence or of work. Until the fund answers (OQ-02), the canton is asked only of employees living in Switzerland. It depends on address_country from FEAT-02. Registered partnerships, and portal behaviour for Divorced or Widowed, are still open.

stories.title: Name and date of birth for the pension fund
stories.i_want: to receive the new employee's first name, last name and date of birth
stories.so_that: I can register the employee for occupational pension without the registration being rejected for missing required fields
stories.priority_reason: These are required fields of the pension fund registration; if any is missing, the portal rejects the registration and highlights the field (F-SC-015), which blocks the registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: First and last name are always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is filling in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their first name and their last name; neither can be left empty, and both are made available for the pension fund registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is always asked and required as a date
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is filling in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their date of birth as a day, month and year (shown as DD.MM.YYYY, e.g. 14.02.1990); it cannot be left empty and is made available for the pension fund registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Each detail is asked only once
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has given their name and date of birth
acceptance_criteria.when: another part of the onboarding or another receiving party needs the same detail
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not asked for it again; the earlier answer is reused.

stories.title: Civil status from the pension fund's list
stories.i_want: to receive the employee's civil status as one of the values my registration accepts
stories.so_that: I can register the employee and know whether spouse details apply
stories.priority_reason: Civil status is a required pension fund field; without it the registration is blocked (F-SC-010, F-SC-015). It is also an input for source tax (F-TR-029, F-TR-030).

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is filling in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their civil status; it cannot be left empty and is made available for the pension fund registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Only the pension fund's civil status values are offered
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for their civil status
acceptance_criteria.then: they can choose exactly one of: Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, as the pension fund lists them; no other values are offered. How employees in a registered partnership or another status (e.g. separated) answer is open (OQ-03).

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is reused for source tax and HR
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has given their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the source tax decision or the source tax questions need it
acceptance_criteria.then: the same answer is reused and the employee is not asked again.

stories.title: Spouse's date of birth for married employees
stories.i_want: to receive the spouse's date of birth for every married employee, and only for them
stories.so_that: the registration of married employees is not blocked and no spouse data is collected without need
stories.priority_reason: The portal blocks the registration of a married employee without the spouse's date of birth (F-SC-016).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's date of birth is asked and required only for married employees
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has given their civil status
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked for their husband's or wife's date of birth (DD.MM.YYYY), cannot leave it empty, and it is made available for the pension fund registration; for any other civil status it is not asked. Whether the fund needs spouse data for Divorced or Widowed is open (OQ-04).

examples.name: Tomás, married, wife lives with him in Winterthur (F-TR-030)

stories.title: Canton for employees living in Switzerland
stories.i_want: to receive a Swiss canton for the employee
stories.so_that: I can complete the required canton field of the registration
stories.priority_reason: Canton is a required pension fund field; without it the registration is blocked (F-SC-006, F-SC-015).

acceptance_criteria.title: Canton is asked and required only of employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has given the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked for their canton, cannot leave it empty, and it is made available for the pension fund registration; employees living outside Switzerland are not asked, until the fund clarifies whether it means the canton of residence or of work and what applies to employees living abroad (OQ-02).

acceptance_criteria.title: Only the fund's Swiss cantons are offered
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for their canton
acceptance_criteria.then: they can choose exactly one of the 26 cantons the pension fund lists: Aargau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Basel-Landschaft, Basel-Stadt, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva, Glarus, Graubünden, Jura, Lucerne, Neuchâtel, Nidwalden, Obwalden, Schaffhausen, Schwyz, Solothurn, St. Gallen, Thurgau, Ticino, Uri, Valais, Vaud, Zug, Zurich.
